text:
sam: Quick question — we keep getting questions from support about preview vs apply behavior for runtime configs. Can we agree on the contract for the preview API and what telemetry we emit when people hit it?

marta: +1. The console 'preview' currently returns a diff and a simulated route distribution, but no telemetry that a preview happened. That makes it hard to audit who tested what.

dyson: I wanted to avoid preview generating the same metrics as a real rollout (would skew SLO/alerts). But we should log an audit event and sampling telemetry.

sam: Exactly. Proposal: preview is a non-mutating dry-run. Emits: 1) an audit event (who, config id, preview payload), 2) a preview-execution telemetry counter (sampled at 1%). No effect on quota/routing metrics or SLO dashboards.

ops-bot: Note: deploy-bot will reject preview calls that try to mutate protected keys (e.g., routing.weights) — just FYI.

laura: For the API we should be explicit — POST /config/preview returns {diff, routeSimulation, warnings}. Example:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/configs/preview \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -d '{"config": {...}, "target": "staging"}'
```

laura: That response should include a preview_id we can link to audit logs.

ankur: On telemetry sampling: 1% sounds fine for volume, but ops needs a 100% sink for previews that affect high-sensitivity keys (auth, quotas). Maybe a flag: preview.sensitive=true that forces full logging.

marta: Good call. We can mark keys as sensitive in the config schema and have the preview endpoint escalate sampling for those.

ryan: UX question — in console we should show a colored badge: "Preview — not applied" + link to preview_id so platform can replay checks. Also allow a one-click transition from preview->canary that preserves the exact applied diff.

sam: On atomicity: some teams expect apply to be transactional across services. We need to document that apply is eventually consistent per region; it's best-effort atomic within a single config service; cross-region fans out and may be delayed. Should we add a preflight validation step that simulates the eventual state and rejects impossible constraints?

dyson: We already run server-side validation for schema and routing consistency. Preflight simulation would be the same codepath as preview but run synchronously with apply and fail the apply if simulation rules break. I'm +1 if it doesn't add huge latency.

laura: Implementation detail: add a header X-Config-Apply-Mode: preview|preflight|apply. Preflight runs the simulator with 5s timeout and returns 409 with details if constraints fail.

ankur: For dashboards: add a "pending changes" timeline in Config History: previews (readonly), preflights (failed/passed), applies (ok/rolled back). Telemetry should attach preview_id/preflight_id to any emitted signals.

marta: Rollout UX: preserve the preview-generated cohort sampling when user promotes to canary. Also record the delta so audit+cost teams can estimate impact before apply.

ryan: Edge case: someone previews a config that causes quota routing to shift to a small pool and then applies — we need an automated pre-apply cost check. Can we run a quick cost-estimation and fail apply if expected qps on small pool > pool capacity?

dyson: We have capacity signals; we can add a lightweight check against pool capacity with a conservative headroom margin. If it fails, return actionable guidance (e.g., increase pool size or enable fallback routing).

sam: OK action items: 1) API: define preview response with preview_id + sampling rules (laura), 2) backend: implement audit event + sampled preview telemetry + forced logging for sensitive keys (dyson/ankur), 3) console: preview badge + promote-to-canary preserving cohort (ryan/marta), 4) add preflight header semantics and 5s timeout + preflight failure codes (laura/dyson).

marta: I'll open a tiny RFC doc with the wire format and telemetry events. Assign owners and we'll sync next tues.

sam: Thanks — tagging folks: @dyson @laura @ankur @ryan. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Reminder: next config deploy window is Tue 02:00 UTC; preflight tests must finish before then to be included.
